title: A key written with few symbols (digits in any base, clock hours, Roman numerals): smallest window and number of distinct key values on 666,993 keyword tableaux, no rule for the key
k4_result: 13,339,856 settings (666,993 alphabets x 5 layouts x 4 views; 6,669,928 key streams computed, a view and its negative share the window numbers). Smallest circular window holding all 24 key values: 12 (3 key streams: BAGGIT~cols and CAGIT~cols M/A-Z Beaufort, values 8-19; ISOTRIMORPHOUS~keyed M/M Vigenere); none at 11 or less. Fewest distinct values: 8 (4 streams); none at 7 or fewer. Most clue letters in a window of 5/8/10/12/16 values: 19/21/23/24/24. Most on any 2/3/4/7 values: 13/17/18/23. Most values that are digits 0-9 (either sign): 22 of 24; smallest base holding all 24 from 0: 14 (13 streams). Most Roman numeral key letters (I V X L C D M, key letter read in A-Z, KRYPTOS or the tableau alphabet, either sign): 19 of 24. The key values of the top 20 settings show no number pattern. Clue blocks alone: EASTNORTHEAST fits a window of 5 on one tableau (OYSTERWIFE~keyed, A-Z/M Beaufort: 7 4 3 6 6 7 7 4 6 5 6 6 7), but on that tableau the BERLINCLOCK values are scattered over the whole alphabet (0 1 7 24 25 4 12 18 17 18 16); BERLINCLOCK alone fits a window of 5 (5 streams).
controls: 50 shuffled K4s, same alphabets. Smallest window: 10 (1 shuffle), 11 (4), 12 (12), 13 (20), 14 (13): 17 of 50 reach K4's 12 and 5 beat it. Fewest distinct values: 7 (2), 8 (29), 9 (19). Window of 5/8/10/12 cover: best 16-19 / 19-22 / 21-24 / 22-24 (K4's 19 in a window of 5 is equalled by 4 shuffles; 24 in a window of 12 by 17). Any 3 values: 15-17 (K4's 17 equalled by 1). Any 7 values: 22-24. Digits 0-9: 19-23. Base: 12-16 (15 shuffles lower than K4). Roman letters: 18-21 (12 shuffles higher). BERLINCLOCK alone: window 4-7 (6 shuffles lower). EASTNORTHEAST alone: window 6-9 in the 50 (K4's 5 not reached); a side check on 300 more shuffles gave 5 in 6 of 300 (2%), 6 in 36, 7 in 100, 8 in 123. This was the only one of 24 compared numbers where K4 was ahead of all 50 controls.
planted: 4/4 flagged with the exact key values (random non-periodic keys on dictionary tableaux among all 666,993 alphabets): digits 0-9 on PREVIOUS M/M Vigenere (window 10; 11 key streams at 10 or less and 38 at 12 or less, all neighbouring alphabets such as PREMIOUS, where K4 has 0 and 3); base-12 digits on WHOSE M/A-Z Beaufort (window 12; 3 streams at 12 or less, one chance stream at 11 ranked above it); clock hours 1-12 on SHA~cols KRYPTOS/M Vigenere (window 11, first); Roman letters read in A-Z on NAMES~cols A-Z/M Vigenere (6 distinct values, 24 of 24 Roman by name, first; 20 streams with 7 or fewer values). Ranked first outright: 2 of 4; the other two were tied or passed by 2 different keys.
scope_limits: Says nothing about keys that use most of the alphabet (more than about 11 consecutive values, or more than 7 scattered values). A base-12 or clock-hour key (window 12) is NOT separated from chance by the window alone: 17 of 50 shuffled K4s also have a window of 12 somewhere, and K4 has three such streams; what K4 lacks is the cluster of neighbouring tableaux that a planted key lights up (38 streams for the planted digit key against 3), so bases 12-16 rest on that weaker argument, while a window of 10 or less (digits, bases 2-10) and 7 or fewer values (Roman numerals) are cleanly absent (10 was reached by 1 of 50 shuffles, 7 values by 2). Alphabets: A-Z, KRYPTOS and dictionary keyword alphabets with their two transposition-mixed forms only; a hidden or non-keyword alphabet is not covered. One alphabet against itself, A-Z or KRYPTOS (five layouts); two different keyword alphabets not tested. Additive tableaux only (C-P, C+P and negatives), no multipliers, no transposition before or after, clue positions as published. Numbers written with two symbols per value (two-digit numbers spread over two letters are covered only as digits; a key number larger than 25 reduced mod 26 is not a few-symbol key and is not covered). The single-block results (13 or 11 letters) are far too weak to decide anything alone.

negative.family: Few-symbol keys (digits in a base, clock numerals, Roman numerals) on keyword tableaux
negative.hypothesis: K4's key is a list of numbers written with few symbols (digits in base 2-16, clock hours 1-12 or Roman numeral letters), so on the right keyword tableau the 24 key values forced by the clues fall in a small window of consecutive values or on 7 or fewer values, whatever rule the numbers follow.
negative.scope: 666,993 alphabets (A-Z, KRYPTOS, dictionary keyword alphabets and their two transposition-mixed forms) x 5 layouts x 4 views (C-P, C+P, P-C, -(C+P)) = 13,339,856 settings; smallest circular window of the 24 key values, number of distinct values, cover by windows of 5-16 and by any 2-7 values, digits 0-9 and smallest base for both signs, Roman letters I V X L C D M with the key letter read in A-Z, KRYPTOS or the tableau alphabet; each clue block alone
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: K4's smallest window is 12 (3 streams, none at 11 or less), fewest distinct values 8, most Roman letters 19 of 24, most digits 22 of 24 (controls: 50 shuffled K4s give smallest windows 10-14 with 17 at 12 or less, distinct 7-9, Roman 18-21, digits 19-23; planted 4/4 flagged with the exact key, a planted digit key lights up 38 neighbouring streams at 12 or less where K4 has 3). Windows of 10 or less and 7 or fewer values are cleanly absent; a window of exactly 12 occurs by chance in a third of shuffles, so bases 12-16 are ruled out only by the missing cluster and the patternless key values.

follow_ups: Few-symbol key with a hidden alphabet, exactly: for each layout (M/M, M/A-Z, A-Z/M) decide by constraint search whether ANY alphabet M puts all 24 clue key values in a circular window of w = 2..12 (the community did this only for the window 0-9 in one view). Each clue pair says pos(C) - pos(P) lies in the window; 24 interval constraints on 26 positions with distinct positions, solvable by backtracking; compare the smallest feasible w with 50 shuffled K4s and with planted digit keys on random alphabets.

Cluster test as a general detector: a planted key on one keyword tableau shows almost the same key on dozens of neighbouring keyword alphabets (38 streams for a digit key here). Score every earlier exact test's near-misses by how many neighbouring alphabets share them, K4 against shuffled K4s; this could catch a right method on a keyword that is close to, but not in, the dictionary.
